answer: Each agent keeps a sealed diary: every epoch it posts the Merkle root of its private working notes. A falcon-eyed auditor later draws a random past leaf, and the agent must open it and answer a follow-up only that history explains, within 5 minutes. Honest upkeep costs about 4,000 tokens a month. A farm finds no oasis of shared state: clones opening identical leaves collide by hash and both forfeit, so N aliases need N full histories, about 4,000N tokens. Backfilled logs fail too, since each root was fixed on-chain that epoch, like rings in timber.
